chapter_title: Concerning the Interpretation of the Fourteen [Gre

spiritual_reading.full_translation:
Know that in the ordered fullness of interior light there abides a complete acknowledgment made up of a sufficient series of fundamental falsities and the operative powers that proceed from them, together with the twofold proceeding by which influx is directed and then received. Divine love consecrates these things and gives them life within their recipient forms, so that the whole becomes a full complex: what is sufficient for operation conjoined with the marriage of willing and understanding.

There is also a sufficient complement of sustaining powers that uphold the entire weight of the created effect in the lowest degree, together with the two principal origins from which those powers are derived. This is the complete acknowledgment that has been uttered: worship brought to fullness by a complete measure of supplications, through which the created order in its lowest degree is held in stability.

Further, there are complete interior states of light within the highest ordering, and the inner church has spoken of them in confession because they are set forth within doctrine concealed from what is merely external and not yet disclosed. This concealed doctrine is established and made firm; it endured the assault of evil, and nothing in what opposes could be equal to it or prevail against it. Within these things there is a hidden fullness.

Therefore Divine truth proceeding from Divine good was sent forth and took its station with power in the midst of these living ordered realities. It is the beneficent origin of all interior states and of all holy truths conjoined into one. It became the leader and governing wisdom in the created order, according to the likeness of the Divine itself, which is the source and lord of all orderly dispositions. Thus the whole created effect in the lowest degree is held together by their united willing, for their counsel and their thought are one, even to the completion of the process.

paragraph_translations.translation: Know that within the ordered fullness of interior light there abides the complete acknowledgment: a sufficient series of fundamental falsities, together with the operative powers that arise to combat and restrain them, and with the twofold proceeding by which influx is directed and then received. Divine love consecrates these things and gives them life within their recipient forms. Thus the whole becomes complete: what is sufficient for operation conjoined with the marriage of willing and understanding.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS the idea that a complete ordering includes both a sufficient series of operations and a twofold proceeding that makes the complex whole.
paragraph_translations.notes: The phrase about “praises” and “great aeons of light” is forced into the sense of complete acknowledgment within ordered interior states; the source text is fragmentary but the functional grouping (five plus two) yields a coherent sufficiency conjoined with a duality.

paragraph_translations.translation: There is also a sufficient complement of sustaining powers that uphold the entire weight of the created effect in the lowest degree, together with the two principal origins from which those powers proceed. This is the complete acknowledgment that has been uttered: worship made full by a complete measure of supplications, through which the created order is held in stability and connection.
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES by expanding from the first complete complex to the sustaining powers and their two origins.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Universe” is taken as the total effect in the natural degree; “fourteen prayers” is rendered as fullness of supplication completing worship.

paragraph_translations.translation:
There are complete interior states of light within the highest ordering, and the inner church speaks of them in confession because they are laid out within doctrine that is concealed from what is merely external and not yet disclosed. This concealed doctrine is established and made firm; it bore the assault of evil, and nothing in what opposes could equal it or prevail against it. Within these things there is a hidden fullness.

Therefore Divine truth proceeding from Divine good was sent forth, and it took its station with power in the midst of these living ordered realities. It is the beneficent origin of all interior states and of all holy truths conjoined into one. It became the leader and governing wisdom according to the likeness of the Divine itself, which is the source and lord of all orderly dispositions. Thus the whole created effect is held together by their united willing, for their counsel and their thought are one, even to the completion of the process.
paragraph_translations.connection: SHIFTS from enumerating ordered components to the establishment of concealed doctrine and the descent of governing Divine truth among those ordered states.
paragraph_translations.notes: This paragraph is heavily damaged: references to “Seth,” “land not revealed,” “hidden plenitude,” and “Ambassador” are partially broken; “Ambassador” is treated as Divine truth sent from Divine good. Some transitions may reflect reconstruction rather than explicit wording.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: Coherent as a single spiritual teaching: it moves from a complete ordered complex (sufficiency plus dual proceeding), to sustaining powers and their origins, then to concealed doctrine made firm against evil, culminating in Divine truth from Divine good establishing governance and unity. The main stumble is paragraph 5’s fragmentation, which forces interpretive reconstruction around the hidden doctrine and the sent Divine principle.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential substrate: a functional grouping (5+2=7) presented as an interior anointing/indwelling, with no jurisdictional list-making beyond the numeration.
findings.evidence: Text teaches by what the items DO in the aeons: “they anoint them, living in them… These shall make seven, five plus two.” Even though the nouns are technical (“five elements… sons of the First Man… call and the hearing”), the spiritual reading’s method (a complete complex formed by 5+2) is anchored in the text’s functional claim of indwelling/anointing rather than in governance titles. The reader notes only that the phrase “praises… great aeons of light” is ‘forced,’ but the internal logic is stable and not a narrative break.

findings.diagnosis: Mostly correspondential but with mild systematizing pressure: the paragraph shifts from indwelling/anointing (¶3) to cosmic support/establishment language; still, it remains functional (supporting weight; establishing universe) rather than administrative jurisdiction. No clear insertion seam.
findings.evidence: Key verbs are functional/cosmic: “support all the weight of the universe… by which the universe is established.” The named entities (“five sons of the Living Spirit… Living Spirit and the First Man, their fathers”) are not arranged as offices with territories; they are presented as structural causes/supports. The spiritual reading continues smoothly here and does not report a narrative stumble beyond interpreting “fourteen prayers” as fullness; that is consistent with the text’s explicit didactic recapitulation: “These are the fourteen praises… made of fourteen prayers.”

findings.diagnosis: Genuine difficulty from damage plus a probable seam where a mythic/administrative christological promotion overlays a prior correspondential point about hidden stability. The reading stumbles because the text jumps from ‘land not revealed/hidden plenitude’ (functional/experiential concealment) into a titulary enthronement of an ‘Ambassador… good father… leader… great king’ (governance/authority register) without a clean connective in the damaged line.
findings.evidence: The reader flags: “heavily damaged… transitions may reflect reconstruction,” listing exactly the disruptive tokens: “Seth,” “land not revealed,” “hidden plenitude,” “Ambassador.” In the Coptic text the shift is visible: first a concealment/stability motif—“explained… in the land that is not revealed… established and made firm… bore up under the enemy… The hidden plenitude that is within them”—then an abrupt enthronement/governance chain: “the Ambassador who came from the Father… came and stood firm in the midst of these… he is called the good father of all the aeons and gods… leader and a great king… lord of all these counsels. This universe is held together by their will… their counsel and their thought are one.” The titles (“good father… leader… great king… lord”) and the administrative abstraction (“counsels”) are exactly the register that forces the spiritual reader into importing ‘Divine truth from Divine good’ to bridge the gap. Removing the enthronement material would leave a coherent correspondential statement about concealed doctrine/land and its firmness against the enemy.
findings.scope: Excise the enthronement/governance overlay beginning at the first clear titulary marker and running to the end of the paragraph: “the hidden plenitude that [is within them] the Ambassador who came from the Father, the [sent forth] He came and stood firm in the midst of these [Living Word]: he is called the good father of [all] the ae[ons and gods] who are holy and conjoined. He has become leader and a great king after the likeness of the first Father, the lord of all these cou[nse]ls. This universe is held together by their will [and their counsel and their thought are one] to the end of all things.”

textual_criticism.summary: 3 findings: ¶3 and ¶4 read as clean correspondential substrate (no action). ¶5 is mixed due to heavy damage plus an intrusive governance/enthronement overlay centered on the ‘Ambassador’ and royal titles; recommended excision of the titulary block to restore a smoother correspondential narrative about concealed stability/hidden plenitude.

changes_summary: Implemented Finding 3 (¶5) excision: removed the enthronement/governance overlay beginning with “The hidden plenitude that [is within them] the Ambassador…” through the end of the paragraph (“…to the end of all things”) to restore a coherent correspondential statement about the concealed land’s firmness against the enemy.
